newsitem.title: ITALY: No mutiny under way in Bangui, says president.
newsitem.headline: No mutiny under way in Bangui, says president.

text.p: President Ange-Felix Patasse of the Central African Republic denied on Saturday that a mutiny was under way by dissident soldiers in the capital Bangui and said common criminals who had escaped were trying to spread panic.
"Nothing abnormal," was his response when asked by Reuters at a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit in Rome about the situation in Bangui.
"It is not a mutiny. Some common law prisoners have escaped and are trying to create panic. That is all," Patasse said.
Witnesses in Bangui said earlier that soldiers had launched a mutiny after forcibly taking weapons from an armoury.
They said French troops and loyalist presidential guards were patrolling the deserted city centre, the scene of serious clashes last May during a similar revolt which was put down by French troops.
Patasse did not reply when asked whether he intended to return to the Central African Republic to deal with the situation.
He made no reference to the events in Bangui when he later addressed the summit. The five-day meeting ends on Sunday.
